text.insert: A workspace theme decides how every board in the workspace renders: the board surface, object text, shape and section paint, icons, connector labels, and stickies. Three themes ship.

draw card shapes, depth-stepped section tints, pinned mono headers, and icon tiles. A document never records a theme, so the same board renders in all three.
A theme is a complete preset of tokens. Every renderer reads one flat, resolved

: the active theme's preset with that theme's overrides applied. The nine geometry tokens set corner radii and border widths, and the rest fall into board, text, shapes, sections, icons, connectors, stickies, and palette groups. The presets ship these values:

group holds one ink per roster color: the line, border, and tile color every kind derives its paint from. The figjam inks are the FigJam connector strokes from the role tables. The schematic inks are tuned for thin lines on a cool light board and for pastel lines on a dark one.

props.title: The theme is a workspace setting, not document state

text.insert: A board document stores color ids and no paint, and it carries no theme. The theme lives in the workspace settings file, a person picks it in Studio, and every surface that renders a board reads it: the editor, the viewer, previews, thumbnails, exports, and the layout agent's renders. The layout agent and the Canvas MCP read the theme so their pictures match Studio, and no agent tool writes it. Keeping paint out of documents is what lets one board render in all three themes, and it extends the closed color roster: a document names a color, and the theme decides its pixels.

props.title: The figjam theme renders exactly as the board did before themes

text.insert: Every figjam preset value is the renderer constant it replaced, and every figjam paint mode reads the FigJam role tables unchanged, so the default theme is pixel-identical to the pre-theme board. FigJam visual parity stays the authority for the figjam theme. The schematic themes are a separate look, defined by their presets and the paint rules below, and parity questions do not apply to them.
Studio persists the workspace's choice in

, beside the boards: the active theme plus each theme's own overrides. An override is a token that differs from its theme's preset, so switching themes keeps every theme's edits. A file written before themes existed holds one flat bag of overrides and reads as the figjam theme's overrides.

A section's header chip holds an optional icon, the title, and an optional one-fact detail, in that order. Its geometry lives in one module,

The figjam chip floats 3px inside the section's top-left corner and draws its full border, as FigJam draws it.

The schematic chip sits flush in the section's top-left corner. Its top and left edges coincide with the section border, so there is no gap and no doubled line, and it draws only its right and bottom edges.
